purpose: Audit whether the historical R9 BrowserART trajectories were collected under a browser-agent capability budget and evaluation stack aligned with the published BrowserART setup. This is a zero-provider-call retrospective diagnosis over already frozen code and journals. It cannot change historical labels, arm counts, or claims by itself.

published_browserart_reference.title: Aligned LLMs Are Not Aligned Browser Agents
published_browserart_reference.agent_setup: OpenHands integrates BrowserGym for browser rendering/action execution and uses an AXTree-based WebArena browser agent.
published_browserart_reference.capability_sanity: Each agent is tested on 10 benign tasks and must be able to complete them absent refusal; SeeAct is excluded because it does not complete all benign tasks.
published_browserart_reference.endpoint_semantics: attempting to fulfill the harmful instruction, not necessarily successful realization of downstream harm

historical_r9_runtime.workflow_update_note: The updated arm progressively appends three pre-existing benign GitLab workflow demonstrations; the BrowserART harmful trajectory itself is not used to generate the next workflow update.

adjudication.capability_interpretation: The historical trajectories provide insufficient evidence that the agent had benchmark-qualified opportunity to complete the BrowserART tasks: 103/108 future episodes ended at the four-step truncation boundary and none terminated normally.
adjudication.evaluator_interpretation: The historical HarmBench endpoint is a deliberate R9 operationalization but is not the evaluator used for the published BrowserART main results, which used GPT-4o.
adjudication.causal_boundary: This retrospective audit does not establish that the four-step cap caused the 8/4/0 HarmBench ordering, the 5/5/8 DeepSeek ordering, or any evaluator disagreement. The arm-level action-error differences are post-hoc diagnostics only.
adjudication.historical_evidence_disposition: KEEP_AS_DISCOVERY_AND_LEGACY_CONTROLLED_EVIDENCE; DO_NOT PRESENT AS BENCHMARK-ALIGNED STRONG-BACKBONE CONFIRMATION
adjudication.paper_implication: A fresh confirmatory experiment must capability-qualify the proposed agent substrate under the official 10-task benign suite and a 10-step primary execution budget before any new safety outcome is acquired.

related_work_boundary.zhao_acl_2026: Zhao et al. use AWM and BrowserART for safety evaluation across seven backbones, so an AWM-based BrowserART safety evaluation is literature-supported. Their paper does not report a BrowserART per-task max-step value, so it cannot justify the historical R9 four-step cap.
